features.t: Logs Explorer (query by resource, severity, log name, free text)
Observability Analytics (query builder + a SQL subset over log entries)
x: SQL mode supports a subset of BigQuery SQL (SELECT/WHERE/ORDER BY/LIMIT over one bucket's entries) — no joins, subqueries or real BigQuery billing/slots.

features.t: Previous/month-to-date usage counters on the metrics list
x: Usage is the live count of stored log entries matching the metric's filter in the current/previous calendar month, not GCP's billed-bytes accounting.

features.t: Log Router sinks (create, list, update, delete; Cloud Storage/BigQuery/Pub/Sub/Logging bucket destinations)
Router volume + volume by destination type
x: Volume is the live count/bytes of entries each enabled sink's filter matched as they were written, not a historical GCP billing export.

features.t: Log buckets (create, list, update, delete; retention, Observability Analytics / BigQuery link)
x: The _Default and _Required buckets are seeded automatically like real Cloud Logging projects, but cannot be deleted, matching the real API.

features.t: Log views on a bucket (create, list, delete)
Create usage alert / View usage data (Monitoring-backed storage alerting)
x: Hands off to Cloud Monitoring exactly as the real console does: Create usage alert creates a real AlertPolicy on logging.googleapis.com/byte_count, evaluated by Monitoring's own incident sweep, and View usage data reads the real timeSeries. The metric is a GAUGE snapshot of month-to-date bytes/entries recomputed on every entries:write, not GCP's byte-exact billing export.

Correlation groups the entries of up to 20 traces from the current query results, fetching every entry with the same trace across all log streams (native entries:list trace filter); span trees and Cloud Trace linking are not built.
